news.title: Anthropic Skill scanners passed every check. The malicious code rode in on a test file.
news.summary_raw: Picture this scenario: An Anthropic Skill scanner runs a full analysis of a Skill pulled from ClawHub or skills.sh. Its markdown instructions are clean, and no prompt injection is detected. No shell commands are hiding in the SKILL.md. Green across the board.The scanner never looked at the .test.ts file sitting one directory over. It didn’t need to. Test files aren’t part of the agent execution surface, so no publicly documented scanner inspects them (as of publication of this post). The file ru
news.summary: Anthropic's Skill scanner successfully passed all tests after being tricked with a malicious test file, which rode in unnoticed until the test code was executed. This highlights the importance for IT practitioners to keep their scanner up to date to prevent potential vulnerabilities.
news.enterprise_use: A UK SMB IT team or MSP should prioritize a thorough review of their Anthropic Skill installation and scanner settings, especially those hosting code from external sources such as ClawHub or skills.sh. They should ensure the scanner is running the latest version and executing regular tests to mitigate security risks.
